source_text:
ἀναπόδιστον τιμωρίαν. Ταμιεῖα κοιλίας ἐστὶν ὁ νοῦς, ἡ καρδία, καὶ ἡ γνῶ σις, ἔνθα
πάντα τὰ θεῖά τε καὶ ἀσεβῆ ἐναποτίθενται διδάγματα· ὥσπερ δέ τις λύχνον ἅψας,
τῶν ἐν τοῖς ταμιείοις κειμένων εὑρεῖν τι βούλεται, οὕτως ὁ Κύ ριος τῷ φωτὶ τῆς
γνώσεως αὐτοῦ ἐρευνᾷ τὰ ταμιεῖα τῶν ἐν λόγοις καὶ πράξεσιν ἀνθρώπων· τοῖς δὲ
τὴν γνῶσιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἐπισταμένοις ἀνθρώποις, φῶς ἐστιν αὐτοῖς· εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς
τοῦ Κυρίου, ἡ γνῶσις τοῦ Κυρίου ἐστὶ, τὸ δὲ φῶς τοῦ Κυρίου ἡ πνοὴ τῶν ἀνθρώπων,
ἄρα ἡ γνῶσις τοῦ Κυρίου πνοὴ τῶν ἀν θρώπων ἐστί· τὸν δὲ ἐν ἀγνοίᾳ διάβολον
φαίνειν δο κοῦντα, λύχνον ὠνόμασεν ἐκκενοῦντα τὸν νοῦν τῶν ἀγαθῶν γνώσεων,
καὶ μετασχηματιζόμενον εἰς ἄγγε λον φωτός· ἐπεὶ δὲ τὸ φῶς τοῦ Κυρίου, οὐχ
εἵλαντο γνῶναι οὐδὲ πορεύεσθαι ἐν αὐτῷ, τὴν ἄγνοιαν ὡς φῶς ἐλογίζοντο οἱ
ἀσεβεῖς· εἰ δὲ τὴν ἄγνοιαν ὡς φῶς εἶχον, δηλονότι καὶ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ τῆς ἀγνοίας
ἐφευρε τοῦ διαβόλου ἔπραττον· οἱ δὲ τῇ ἀγνοίᾳ αὐτοῦ
pass_a_gloss: Absurd retribution. Mind functions as belly’s treasury, heart’s vault, and knowledge’s depository—where sacred and profane teachings are stored. Like lighting a lamp to rummage through pantry stores, the Lord probes human speech and action with His knowing light. Those possessing His knowing light have it as illumination. Thus: Lord’s light = Lord’s knowing; Lord’s light = human breath; thus Lord’s knowing = human breath. The ignorance demon, masquerading, is dubbed a lamp draining mind of good knowledge, shifting into light’s angel form. Since Lord’s light went unknown, unwalked in, the godless mistook ignorance for light. Holding ignorance as light, they enacted the ignorance demon’s devised deeds; consorting with his ignorance, they’ll share his eternity long fate. But those aligned with Lord’s knowing dwell with the Lord. He invalidates irrational animal sacrifice—divine sacrifice is spirit crushed. If Lord’s works are holy and correct, and mind is among His works, God made the mind straight and clean; we must keep it so from evil attacks. He placed the polluted, shared house opposite the open corner—if that house is sin, the open corner is virtue, the angle of contemplative practice lit by righteousness’ sun. Paul called the Jewish high priest a defiled wall, to be blinded by God; Jesus called Pharisees defiled graves. The stone rejected by builders, made head of the corner, is Christ. Common means not of the one God. Secret giving: right hand gives, left unaware—it provokes fierce anger on judgment day against those who deny help to the poor. The giants’ synagogue is evil and ignorance; giants are demons; the wanderer from justice rests in major sins. Better to be alone than to join such folk; David says he saw God in the holy place as in a dry, trackless, thirsty land. Virtue makes the soul a wilderness, empty of old sinful habits rooted in deceit; thus the devil finds no rest there, wandering dry places seeking it but failing, since he rules over those who luxuriate in water and fleshly delight. Wisdom’s ways are sheltered rooms in her house—so the quarrelsome, talkative, angry woman is wickedness, making her companion like her. Divine wisdom dwells in the heart of the just and wise; fools revile her to ruin her. Wisdom is a strong city where the wise live, demolishing reasonings and every proud thing raised against God’s knowledge—those strongholds being souls held by evil spirits and wicked men who defy divine knowledge; the wise climbs them, sees their false safety, and by wisdom overthrows them. pass_b_english:
An absurd punishment. The mind is the storehouse of the belly, the heart, and knowledge; in it are laid up all divine teachings as well as impious doctrines. Just as one who lights a lamp seeks to find something among the things stored in the pantries, so the Lord, with the light of His knowledge, searches the storehouses of human words and deeds. To those people who know the Lord’s knowledge, it is light for them. Therefore, if the Lord’s light is the Lord’s knowledge, and the Lord’s light is the breath of humanity, then the Lord’s knowledge is the breath of humanity. The demon who appears in ignorance, pretending to be something, He has named a lamp that empties the mind of good knowledges and transforms itself into an angel of light. Since, however, the Lord’s light was not chosen to be known or walked in by them, the impious reckoned ignorance as light. If they indeed held ignorance as light, then clearly they also practiced the works invented by the demon of ignorance; those who journeyed with his ignorance will be with him into the ages of ages. But those who are with the Lord’s knowledge will be with the Lord. He casts out this statement regarding the sacrifice offered through irrational beasts; for a sacrifice to God is a spirit broken in pieces. If holy and right works are the Lord’s works, and one of His works is the mind,

The mind was rightly created by God, pure and upright, and we are obligated to preserve it in that state against the evil influences that come upon us. He set the defiled and common house in opposition to the open-air corner; but if the defiled and common house is wickedness, then the open-air corner is virtue—the very angle of virtue. This is the practice of contemplation in action, touching and enlightened by the sun of righteousness. Paul also spoke well when he called the high priest of the Jews a defiled wall, to be struck blind by God. Likewise, the Savior in the Gospels called the Pharisees defiled tombs. And well did he say in verse 17.216, upon the corner: “Here lies the stone rejected by the builders, which has become the cornerstone; and this is Christ.” Now, what is common is what does not belong to the one God. Secret giving is when the right hand acts and the left hand does not know; it stirs up a strong wrath against itself on the day of judgment, the one who withholds aid from the needy. The synagogue of the giants is wickedness and ignorance; for the giants are the demons. This means that the one who strays from the path of righteousness will find rest in great sins. It is better to be solitary than to keep company with such as these; and David says: “In a desolate, impassable, and waterless land, thus have I appeared before you in the holy place.”

The earth is now a desert where virtue dwells in the soul, uninhabited by the old human passions that once dwelled there—those corrupting impulses that once ruled according to the former deceitful desires. For this reason, the devil finds no rest in it, since he wanders wearily through waterless places seeking repose, yet finds none; for he is king over all who dwell in the waters, that is, over those who rest and indulge in carnal pleasures. Again: the paths of wisdom are the sheltered dwellings of her house. If this is so, then surely the warlike, gossiping, wrathful woman is wickedness itself—the kind that makes the one who lives with her become warlike, gossipy, and irritable. Wisdom of the Lord rests in the heart of a righteous, wise person; but foolish men slander her in order to destroy her. Wisdom is a fortified city, within which the wise dwell, tearing down reasonings and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God—of which the fortified cities, says the text, are those souls subdued and conquered by impious demons and wicked men, who exalt themselves against the knowledge of God. When the wise man ascends this stronghold and sees their supposed security, he, by means of such wisdom, surrounds and overthrows it.
